lore.summary: Nick says VGDB grew from his own master lists, became vgdb.io, and in2015 focused on North American Nintendo/Sega/Atari/PlayStation/Xbox releases before planned regions/systems expansion.

evidence.quote: all games released in North America
I’ll also open the database to additional systems

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick describes a box-art search interface, owned/not-owned tracking, full system lists and individual releases; these are dated reported features, not a current website audit.

evidence.quote: keep track of which games you own and which games you don’t own

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick says he added his10,000th game the previous week; no named milestone title or independent count verification.

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick dates his collecting start to2005, age18, with400 different cartridge-only NES games for$800. Billion dollars of fun is a value joke, not a valuation.

evidence.quote: 400 different NES games. They were card only
a billion dollars with the fun

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick frames organization, knowing where items are, and treating games as cultural artifacts as his collecting-versus-hoarding distinction; not a clinical definition.

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: At roughly5,000 games, separate text files became disorganized; Nick describes VGDB as his solution, including acquisition date and condition records.

evidence.quote: when I got it and the condition

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick's nostalgic favorite is NES, completed in2009; current collecting interests include Wii, DS and perhaps GBA.

evidence.quote: nearest and dearest to my heart is the regular Nintendo
probably the Wii and the DS

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick names CIB North American Stadium Events and gray/gold NWC among valued collection pieces; their status is reported, not authenticated.

evidence.quote: stadium events complete in box, the North American version

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick says his GameCube interactive demo set has35 discs; most came within months, but January2002 took three years to find.

evidence.quote: January 2002 disc, which took me three years

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick treasures an Xbox Oddworld copy signed by Lorne Lanning; raw Munch of Saddusy is provisionally normalized, not audio-verified.

evidence.quote: signed by the designer, Lorne Lanning

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick says Jack Thompson signed his GTA3 copy and was personally respectful/saw the humor, despite the hosts' hostile wider view. The episode's legal-history claim is not independently verified.

evidence.quote: personally sign a copy of Grand Theft Auto 3
very nice and respectful to me
He saw the humor in it

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick values sets he completed piece by piece, while acknowledging several bought together.

evidence.quote: I didn’t just buy the entire set all at once
which I have done in the past

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick reports an$11,000 US CIB GBC set purchase with International Superstar Soccer99 missing and later obtained separately. No standalone ISS99 price is given.

evidence.quote: It was missing one game, which I’d since gotten

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick says the family skipped SNES for N64, explaining collection priorities rather than dislike; he lists admired SNES games and plans eventual completion.

evidence.quote: I still love the Super Nintendo

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Kat says Instagram connects her with collectors and can let her collection be taken more seriously than some local interactions; no general claim about every woman or local shop.

evidence.quote: There aren’t a whole lot of girls that collect where I am
maybe don’t get taken as seriously locally

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick describes an empty-N64-box trade with Retro Game Trader and a shoutout that reportedly gained about300 followers.

evidence.quote: I sent him a bunch of empty N64 boxes

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick says popular recognizable franchises drew excitement, including Zelda and the explicitly numbered Mega Man examples; these are post subjects, not an acquisition list.

evidence.quote: not necessarily the rarest but the most popular games
Mega Man 1 through 6, Mega Man X2, X3

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick reports about20 Instagram trades, including one delayed shipment that was ultimately sent without further issue; Kat says she has not yet traded there.

evidence.quote: she shipped it and there were no issues
I actually still have not done a trade on Instagram

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: The participants describe intuition, reputation, shoutouts and send-first arrangements as informal trade safeguards. These are historical opinions, not guarantees that follower counts make a trade safe.

evidence.quote: There’s always going to be a slight risk
maybe they send first and then you send second
there is still feedback going on

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Kat describes Instagram as her first online collecting-social outlet; Nick says he was active on forums2005–2009 and still watches them; Johnny describes more recent Instagram adoption.

evidence.quote: Instagram was kind of my first endeavor
between 2005 and I started to wind down on forums around 2009
for the last, you know, six months

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Johnny's old-man/grandpa/100-years-old lines are jokes; the dialogue also says37, but do not convert jokes into verified ages or biography.

evidence.quote: the old man of the podcast

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Kat discusses what she and husband John might do with their jointly built collection after one dies; not a current sale or actual bereavement.

evidence.quote: we would either keep the collection
we’ve done so much of it together

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick has no formal or written succession plan and imagines brother Matt selling the collection to help family.

evidence.quote: I don’t have a plan, a formal plan, or a written plan

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Johnny describes an unwritten conversation with wife/friend about future collection sale;15% was offered and declined, not a binding completed arrangement or legal instrument.

evidence.quote: I told him he could take, you know, 15%, but he said he wouldn’t
No, I’ve talked to my wife and I talked to my buddy

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: At hypothetical full market value Nick refuses and Kat leans no because of memories, while Johnny would consider selling, perhaps keeping SNES and continuing to collect.

evidence.quote: I don’t know if I could part with the Super Nintendo games
You would still continue to collect

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick might consider two-to-three times market value but gives no firm threshold; Kat likewise qualifies her earlier no as untested without a real offer.

evidence.quote: between two and three times market value
I really don’t know where the cutoff is
you never know if somebody came in

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick returns to Mario Kart7 on3DS; he cannot play Fallout4 now and hopes for Super Mario Maker after moving and obtaining WiiU equipment.

evidence.quote: I always go back to Mario Kart 7
Unfortunately, I’m not going to be able to play it
Hopefully, I’ll be playing Super Mario Maker soon

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Nick likely declines the Smash/Splatoon WiiU bundle because its games are digital; this is an intention, not a failed or completed purchase.

evidence.quote: they’re digital copies of the games

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.

lore.summary: Johnny likes digital convenience and imagines a finite physical-game collecting endpoint; digital-versus-physical is suggested for a later show, not resolved here.

evidence.quote: I wish all of my current stuff was digital
there would be a finite stop on collecting
maybe we’ll touch on digital versus physical in another show

speaker.basis: Named participants and question-answer continuity; undiarized source, no audio verification.
